The invention relates to a homogeneous, solid, particulate, urea ammonium sulphate-based composition comprising urea ammonium sulphate and a urease inhibitor of the phosphoric triamide type, wherein the urea ammonium sulphate-based composition is further characterized by the application of one or more of the following measures: (a) it comprises 5 weight % or less, relative to the total weight of the composition, of one or more alkaline or alkaline-forming inorganic or organic compounds capable of interacting with ammonium sulphate; (b) the urease inhibitor of the phosphoric triamide type is present in solid particulate form; and/or (c) an anticaking and/or moisture-repellent coating is applied to the urea ammonium sulphate particulate material.

The invention also relates to a kit-of-parts composition comprising: (a) one or more alkaline or alkaline-forming inorganic compounds capable of interacting with ammonium sulphate; (b) a urease inhibitor of the phosphoric triamide type in solid particulate or liquid form, preferably wherein the urease inhibitor is N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (nBTPT); and (c) optionally, one or more anticaking and/or moisture-repellent compounds.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a homogeneous, solid, particulate composition based on urea ammonium sulphate. The composition contains urea ammonium sulphate in combination with a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor. By incorporating the urease inhibitor into the solid particulate material, the composition is designed to reduce ammonia losses that may occur when urea-containing fertilizers are applied to soil and are exposed to urease activity.

In one embodiment, the composition contains only a limited amount of alkaline or alkaline-forming compounds that are capable of interacting with ammonium sulphate. In particular, the amount of such compounds may be 5 weight % or less, based on the total weight of the composition. Limiting the presence of these alkaline materials can help maintain the stability and effectiveness of the urea ammonium sulphate-based composition.

The phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor may be included in the composition in solid particulate form. Suitable urease inhibitors include, for example, N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide, also known as nBTPT. The particulate material may further be provided with a coating, such as an anticaking coating or a moisture-repellent coating. Such coatings can improve handling, storage stability, flowability, and resistance to moisture uptake.

The composition has improved properties for reducing ammonia loss caused by urease activity in soil. As a result, it is particularly suitable for use as a fertilizer, especially where efficient nitrogen delivery and reduced nitrogen volatilization are desired. The homogeneous solid particulate form also allows convenient storage, transport, and application using conventional fertilizer equipment.

The invention further includes a method for manufacturing the composition. The method may involve combining urea ammonium sulphate with a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor, optionally in solid particulate form, and optionally applying an anticaking or moisture-repellent coating to the resulting particles. The process may be carried out so as to obtain a homogeneous solid particulate product with stable distribution of the urease inhibitor.

In addition, the invention covers a kit of parts. The kit may include one or more alkaline or alkaline-forming compounds, a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor such as nBTPT, and optionally one or more anticaking or moisture-repellent compounds. Such a kit can be used to prepare, treat, or supplement a urea ammonium sulphate-based fertilizer composition in order to improve its resistance to ammonia loss and enhance its practical performance in agricultural use.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to improved urea ammonium sulphate fertilizer products and to methods for producing them. More particularly, the invention addresses the problem of ammonia loss that occurs when urea-containing fertilizers are applied to soil. In conventional urea ammonium sulphate fertilizers, the urea component may be hydrolyzed by the enzyme urease, which is naturally present in many soils. This hydrolysis can lead to the formation and release of ammonia, causing nitrogen losses, reduced fertilizer efficiency, undesirable odor, and environmental concerns.

To reduce these losses, the invention provides a homogeneous solid particulate fertilizer composition comprising urea ammonium sulphate and a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor. The urease inhibitor is incorporated in such a way that it is distributed uniformly throughout or on the solid fertilizer particles, thereby ensuring reliable performance when the fertilizer is applied to soil. By inhibiting urease activity, the composition slows the conversion of urea into ammonia and helps retain nitrogen in a plant-available form for a longer period.

In certain embodiments, the fertilizer composition may further comprise a limited amount of one or more alkaline compounds. These alkaline compounds may be selected and used in controlled quantities so as to improve the stability or effectiveness of the phosphoric triamide inhibitor without adversely affecting the physical properties of the fertilizer. The composition may also include solid particles containing or consisting of the urease inhibitor, which can be incorporated during manufacture to facilitate accurate dosing and homogeneous distribution.

The invention also provides a manufacturing method for preparing the fertilizer composition. In general, the method involves combining urea ammonium sulphate with the phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor under conditions that produce a solid particulate product. The inhibitor may be added during granulation, prilling, compaction, coating, or another suitable fertilizer production step. The process is designed to obtain a substantially uniform distribution of the inhibitor while maintaining the desired particle size, strength, storage stability, and handling characteristics of the final fertilizer.

In some embodiments, the fertilizer particles may be provided with an anticaking coating, a moisture-repellent coating, or a coating that performs both functions. Such a coating can improve storage and transport properties by reducing caking, dust formation, moisture uptake, or degradation of the active inhibitor. The coating may also help preserve the physical integrity of the particles and contribute to consistent application in the field.

The resulting fertilizer composition is especially useful for efficient nitrogen fertilization. When applied to soil, it reduces urease-driven ammonia volatilization compared with comparable urea ammonium sulphate fertilizers that do not contain the inhibitor. As a result, a greater proportion of the applied nitrogen remains available for crop uptake, which may improve agronomic efficiency, reduce the need for excess fertilizer application, and lessen environmental nitrogen losses.

Accordingly, the invention provides both a stabilized urea ammonium sulphate fertilizer composition and a practical process for manufacturing it. The combination of a homogeneous solid particulate fertilizer matrix, a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor, and optional stabilizing or protective additives results in a product that is well suited for agricultural use and for improving the effectiveness of nitrogen fertilization.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about one particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It helps people understand whether we are discussing something general or something already known. “The sun,” “the world,” “the answer,” and “the moment” all feel more definite and meaningful because of this tiny word.

Although “the” is often unnoticed, it appears everywhere in English writing and speech. It connects ideas, shapes meaning, and makes communication more precise. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.output: A solid particulate fertilizer composition is provided comprising urea ammonium sulphate particles and an effective amount of a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor, preferably N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (nBTPT). The composition exhibits improved reduction of ammonia volatilization relative to corresponding urea ammonium sulphate fertilizer not containing the inhibitor and may provide enhanced nitrogen-use efficiency. counterfactuals.prompt: Write a European patent application summary beginning “The invention relates to…” for a homogeneous urea ammonium sulphate-based composition comprising urea ammonium sulphate and a urease inhibitor, including limitations on alkaline compounds, solid particulate inhibitor form, coating, manufacturing method, and kit of parts.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a homogeneous urea ammonium sulphate-based fertiliser composition comprising urea ammonium sulphate and at least one urease inhibitor, wherein the urease inhibitor is present in solid particulate form and is substantially uniformly distributed throughout the composition. The composition is particularly suitable for reducing ammonia volatilisation after application to soil while maintaining the agronomic and handling properties of urea ammonium sulphate fertilisers.

In one aspect, the composition comprises urea ammonium sulphate and a urease inhibitor selected from phosphoric triamide compounds, preferably N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT), N-(n-propyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NPPT), or mixtures thereof. The urease inhibitor is provided as solid particles, preferably having a controlled particle size distribution to facilitate homogeneous dispersion and to limit degradation during storage.

The composition is preferably essentially free of alkaline compounds, or comprises alkaline compounds only in an amount insufficient to substantially increase the pH of the urea ammonium sulphate phase. In particular embodiments, the composition contains less than 1.0 wt.%, preferably less than 0.5 wt.%, more preferably less than 0.1 wt.% of alkaline compounds, based on the total weight of the composition. The alkaline compounds may include alkali metal hydroxides, alkaline earth metal hydroxides, carbonates, bicarbonates, amines, ammonia-releasing alkaline additives, or other pH-increasing stabilising agents. By limiting such alkaline compounds, incompatibility with the urea ammonium sulphate matrix and undesired changes in fertiliser properties may be avoided.

In a preferred embodiment, the solid particulate urease inhibitor is at least partially coated. The coating may comprise a water-soluble, water-dispersible, biodegradable, polymeric, waxy, lipidic, inorganic, or organic coating material. The coating is selected to reduce direct contact between the urease inhibitor and the urea ammonium sulphate phase during storage, while permitting release of the urease inhibitor after application. Suitable coatings may include polyvinyl alcohol, polyethylene glycol, polysaccharides, lignosulphonates, starch derivatives, cellulose derivatives, fatty acids, waxes, sulphur, mineral coatings, or combinations thereof.

The invention further relates to a method for manufacturing the homogeneous urea ammonium sulphate-based composition, comprising providing a urea ammonium sulphate composition, providing a urease inhibitor in solid particulate form, optionally coating the solid particulate urease inhibitor, and mixing the solid particulate urease inhibitor with the urea ammonium sulphate composition under conditions effective to obtain a substantially homogeneous distribution of the urease inhibitor. The mixing is preferably carried out while avoiding or limiting addition of alkaline compounds. The method may comprise blending the solid particulate urease inhibitor into a liquid, slurry, melt, granulate, prill, powder, or particulate urea ammonium sulphate-based fertiliser composition.

The invention also relates to a kit of parts comprising, in separate containers or compartments, a urea ammonium sulphate composition and a urease inhibitor in solid particulate form, preferably a coated solid particulate urease inhibitor, together with instructions for combining the parts to form a homogeneous urea ammonium sulphate-based fertiliser composition. The kit preferably does not include alkaline stabilising additives, or includes such additives only in limited amounts as defined above.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate the “Field and summary of the invention” text for a fertilizer patent about urea ammonium sulphate granules stabilized with N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide, mentioning reduced urease activity in soil and components for a kit.
counterfactuals.output:
## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to fertilizer compositions and methods for improving nitrogen use efficiency in agricultural soils. More particularly, the invention relates to urea ammonium sulphate fertilizer granules comprising a urease inhibitor, especially N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT), for reducing urease activity in soil and thereby decreasing ammonia volatilization and nitrogen loss. The invention further relates to methods of preparing and using such stabilized fertilizer granules, and to kits comprising components for producing or applying the same.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In one aspect, the invention provides a stabilized fertilizer composition comprising urea ammonium sulphate granules and N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide. The urea ammonium sulphate granules comprise urea and ammonium sulphate in granular form, and the NBPT is present in an amount effective to inhibit or reduce urease activity when the granules are applied to soil. By reducing urease-mediated hydrolysis of urea, the composition can reduce ammonia volatilization, improve retention of plant-available nitrogen in soil, and enhance fertilizer efficiency.

In certain embodiments, the NBPT is coated onto, absorbed into, incorporated within, or otherwise associated with the urea ammonium sulphate granules. The NBPT may be applied to the granules as a liquid formulation, solution, suspension, melt, or coating composition. In some embodiments, the NBPT is combined with one or more carriers, solvents, binders, stabilizers, anti-caking agents, flow aids, dyes, surfactants, or coating materials to improve distribution, storage stability, handling, or release characteristics.

In another aspect, the invention provides a fertilizer granule comprising urea, ammonium sulphate, and NBPT, wherein the granule is configured to deliver nitrogen and sulphur to plants while reducing urease activity in the soil environment following application. In certain embodiments, the granules contain a homogeneous or substantially homogeneous distribution of urea and ammonium sulphate, and the NBPT is present at or near an exterior surface of the granules. In other embodiments, the NBPT is distributed throughout at least a portion of the granule.

In a further aspect, the invention provides a method of reducing urease activity in soil, the method comprising applying to the soil an effective amount of a fertilizer composition comprising urea ammonium sulphate granules stabilized with NBPT. In some embodiments, the method reduces the conversion of urea to ammonia at or near the soil surface, thereby reducing ammonia emissions relative to otherwise comparable urea ammonium sulphate granules lacking NBPT. The composition may be applied before planting, at planting, after planting, as a topdress, broadcast application, banded application, or incorporated application.

In yet another aspect, the invention provides a method for preparing stabilized urea ammonium sulphate granules, comprising providing urea ammonium sulphate granules and contacting the granules with a composition comprising NBPT under conditions sufficient to associate the NBPT with the granules. The contacting step may include spraying, tumbling, mixing, blending, coating, impregnation, or combinations thereof. The resulting granules may be dried, cooled, screened, stored, packaged, or directly applied to soil.

In still another aspect, the invention provides a kit for preparing or applying stabilized urea ammonium sulphate fertilizer granules. The kit may comprise one or more of:  
(a) urea ammonium sulphate granules;  
(b) a urease inhibitor composition comprising N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide;  
(c) a carrier, solvent, coating agent, binder, stabilizer, anti-caking agent, or flow aid;  
(d) instructions for combining the urease inhibitor composition with the granules; and/or  
(e) instructions for applying the stabilized granules to soil in an amount effective to reduce urease activity and improve nitrogen availability to plants.

In certain embodiments, the kit comprises the urea ammonium sulphate granules and the NBPT composition in separate containers, allowing the NBPT to be applied to the granules shortly before use. In other embodiments, the kit comprises pretreated urea ammonium sulphate granules stabilized with NBPT, together with instructions for agricultural application. The kit may further include measuring devices, mixing equipment, spray applicators, packaging materials, or labels indicating recommended application rates and handling procedures.

The compositions, methods, and kits described herein provide a practical means for delivering nitrogen and sulphur nutrients while reducing urease activity in soil and mitigating nitrogen losses associated with urea-containing fertilizers.

counterfactuals.output: A homogeneous, solid, particulate fertilizer composition is provided comprising urea ammonium sulfate (UAS) particles and a phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor distributed substantially uniformly within or on the particles. Also disclosed is a kit-of-parts comprising, as separate components, (i) a urea ammonium sulphate fertilizer comprising urea and ammonium sulphate, and (ii) a urease-inhibitor formulation comprising nBTPT or another phosphoric triamide urease inhibitor, optionally with one or more anticaking, coating, spreading, adhesion-promoting, or moisture-repellent agents, wherein the components are adapted to be combined before application to soil or applied sequentially to provide a stabilized nitrogen- and sulphur-containing fertilizer system.
